title: Point at the running update log when the lock is held
head: 02bddd40c94d
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A second ordinary update overwrites the very transcript the hint tells the user to follow
leads.consequence: The second omarchy-update runs script(1) before attempting the flock. Without -a, script opens /tmp/omarchy-update.log for writing/truncation while the first update is still running. The second then fails the lock and prints the tail command, which points to a transcript now being written concurrently by two script processes, not a clean view of the first update. In the isolated two-update run, first exited 0, second exited 1, and the final transcript contains the first run's completion followed by a truncated fragment of the second run's footer. The second launch can destroy the earlier diagnostics even when its own update does not start. This is a pre-existing writer race, but it directly defeats this PR's recommended way to watch the first run. Acquire the lock before opening/truncating the transcript, or use a distinct transcript per running update and pass that exact path to the lock holder.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1); corroboration; published as finding 1

leads.summary: Other open log-relocation PRs leave the hard-coded hint pointing at the wrong file
leads.consequence: Open #12957 uses ${OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG:-${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/omarchy-update.log}, #8429 uses ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/omarchy}/omarchy-update.log, #12109 uses $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-update/update.log or a private cache fallback, and #7995 uses a state-home update.log. Those four diverged PRs replace the writer's fixed /tmp path. If one is incorporated without adapting this helper, a normal user with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR sees no hint at all when /tmp is absent, or receives a command for an old/unrelated /tmp file while the update writes elsewhere. #12957 also permits an explicit OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG override. In the #12109 per-file merge, the lock helper retains this PR's original hint and the writer uses a different path, with no conflict markers; do not infer that the entire repos merge automatically. Coordinate the log location with the writer or use the exported log path, and account for these open changes.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F4); published as finding 2

leads.summary: The log presence predicate does not identify the process holding the lock
leads.consequence: The lock is in ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}, but the hint only checks whether a fixed /tmp regular file exists. With OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED=1, an update can hold the lock without creating a transcript at all (the changed test uses exactly that path), so the hint is omitted if no old file exists. Conversely, an old file, another account's readable file, a symlink to a regular file, or an unreadable file all pass -f; the user is told to tail a file that may not be written by the running update or that tail cannot read. No runtime error is introduced, and the losing update still exits 1; the added advice is simply unreliable. Tie the hint to the holder's actual transcript path and verify it is the active readable one before presenting it.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2, Q1); folded into finding 1 impact

leads.summary: The added test checks a source string, not whether a contending user sees a usable hint
leads.consequence: Both updater invocations set OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED=1, bypassing the transcript writer, and the test checks only that the already-running line was captured at runtime. Its new assertion searches bin/omarchy-update-lock for a literal string rather than checking update-second.out or arranging a real transcript. A plausible mutation that leaves the string in a comment or an unreachable branch while removing the echo still satisfies the new assertion, even though no user receives the hint. More subtly, the regex does not escape the dot before 'log': mutating the echoed filename to /tmp/omarchy-update_log leaves this assertion passing (rg exit 0 against mutant-update-lock), although the recommendation now names a different file. The head test passes under LC_ALL=C, but it would not guard the new behavior or H1/H3. Set up a private sandbox transcript and assert the second invocation's stdout under present and absent file cases, plus its nonzero exit; separately exercise an actual script(1) logging run.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3); published as optional test note. Regex-dot detail factual (rg pattern unescaped '.') but nitpick; not published

The #12109 per-file merge was checked; repository-wide merges and unrelated PR test suites were not run. The wrong-log behavior follows directly from the independently inspected log writer paths.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The change keeps the exit status at 1 and prints the new line to stdout next to the existing message. From the bar, the menu and the first-run notification, both lines appear in the floating terminal (read from source) above "Failed (exit code 1)! Press any key to close...". No other code parses this output. The PR cherry-picks cleanly onto the current quattro tip. The main problem is that in these real entry paths, the file the hint names no longer holds the running update's output by the time the hint is printed.

### The hint names a log that the refused run has just truncated

`bin/omarchy-update` re-runs itself through `script -qefc ... /tmp/omarchy-update.log` (lines 10-13) before it checks the lock (lines 15-17). util-linux `script` opens the log with `fopen(..., "w")` (`term-utils/script.c`, v2.42.3), which truncates it and writes a new `Script started` header. So when a second `omarchy update` reaches `omarchy-update-lock`, its own `script` has already emptied the running update's transcript and started writing its own.

Isolated run at the head: a first update wrote two progress lines and then waited, and a second `omarchy-update -y` was started the way every entry point starts it, without `OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED` and so through the `script` wrapper (synthetic fixture, every update step stubbed, real util-linux 2.42.3 `script`):

```text
/tmp/omarchy-update.log
  first update running      314 bytes, the first update's progress lines
  second update refused     285 bytes, only:
                              Script started on ... [COMMAND=".../omarchy-update -y " ...]
                              An Omarchy update is already running.
                              Follow it with: tail -f /tmp/omarchy-update.log
                              Script done on ... [COMMAND_EXIT_CODE="1"]
  first update resumes      its next lines appear after 29 NUL bytes; its earlier lines are gone
```

`tail -f` started after the refusal showed only the refused run's own lines until the first update printed again. The log showed the same truncation on the quattro tip with the PR applied. The truncation itself happens on the base and tip without this PR too. The PR adds a hint that depends on that file.

**Impact:**
- The `-f` guard is effectively always true in the real entry paths, because the refused run has just created the file. It only matters when `OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED` is already set, as in the repository test.
- In the #10879 scenario the update may be quiet (for example waiting at the reboot prompt, as the reporter suspected). `tail -f` then shows nothing beyond the refusal it just read.
- Every retry truncates the file again. A retry can erase the "Updating linux initcpios" lines that `omarchy-update-analyze-logs` greps for later in the running update, after the package upgrade (read from source, not run). This part is pre-existing.
- The hint also appears when the lock is held by something that is not an update, such as a leftover child process that inherited the lock (issue #8077, open PR #8081). In a run with a plain `flock` holder and no earlier log, the refused update still printed the hint, and the log held only its own output.

**Suggested change:** Check the lock in `bin/omarchy-update` before the `script` re-run, so a refused run neither truncates the running transcript nor writes its own. A non-blocking probe like the `flock -n "$lock" true` in `omarchy-migrate-notify`, or a small check mode in `omarchy-update-lock`, would do. The hint then points at the running update's real transcript.

### The log path is now hard-coded in a third place

`/tmp/omarchy-update.log` already appears in `bin/omarchy-update` and `bin/omarchy-update-analyze-logs`. Four open PRs move the transcript's default location out of `/tmp`: #7995, #8429, #12109 and #12957. None of them touches the lines this PR adds, so a merge would not flag it. #12109 and #12957 export the path as `OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG`.

**Impact:** After such a merge, the `-f` guard would hide the hint or name a stale leftover file.

**Suggested change:** Read the path from one variable shared with `omarchy-update` and `omarchy-update-analyze-logs`, instead of a third literal.

**Overlap:** Open PR #7434 (shell translation catalogs) rewrites the same `echo "An Omarchy update is already running."` line and the adjacent `grep -q "already running"` test line. A three-way merge of either file with this PR conflicts.

**Optional test improvement:** The new assertion greps the script source (`rg -q 'Follow it with: ...' "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-update-lock"`), and both test updates run with `OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED=1`, so no transcript is created. The test does fail with the three added lines removed. It still passes with the hint wrapped in `if false` or left only as a comment. Asserting the hint in `update-second.out` with a log path the test controls would check the behavior instead.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of `bin/omarchy-update-lock`, `bin/omarchy-update`, the entry points that launch it and the test at head `02bddd40`, the merge base and the quattro tip `7e8d35ef` (none of these files changed on quattro after that tip, as of `fd961e53`), plus util-linux `script.c`. Isolated command-only runs used a synthetic fixture with every privileged and update step stubbed and a real util-linux 2.42.3 `script`. They covered the repository test at the head, base and three mutants, and the two-update and non-update lock-holder scenarios at the head, base, tip and tip with the PR. On the tip, the full `update-lock-test.sh` could not complete in the sandbox (its stay-awake helper requires a root-owned runtime directory chain), so it was run with stay-awake stubbed, where only its first block is meaningful; that block passes with the PR and fails without the hint. The desktop scenario from #10879 (monitor or KVM switch during an update) was not reproduced. Merge checks against related open PRs compared the two changed files only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
